newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco cuts Briton's jail term for drug offence.
newsitem.headline: Morocco cuts Briton's jail term for drug offence.

text.p: Briton David Richards on Wednesday had his sentence for drug trafficking trimmed from five years to four years by a Moroccan appeals court, the official news agency MAP said.
Richards, 37, from Alnwick, Northumberland, was arrested with his wife Jill, 40, in August while embarking from Tangier for Spain with their eight-year old daughter Victoria.
The court of first instance in Tangier, in northern Morocco, sentenced him to five years imprisonment, and fined him 47,000 dirhams ($5,402). His camper vehicle was confiscated.
Richards, who conducted his own defence after his lawyer withdrew, told the court he knew nothing about 222-kg (488 pounds) of cannabis resin found in his vehicle.
Jill Richards, who pleaded not guilty, was acquitted.
Last week, Two British women Sally Louise Griffiths and Claire Louise Martin,arrested for drug trafficking in July, had their jail terms halved after they appealed against a five-year sentence.
